pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Stratford School Academy, a high-achieving inclusive school delivering excellence for all.
Rooted in the local community in the borough of Newham, we aim to provide an inspirational learning journey for every student. It is our firm belief that all of our students have the potential to achieve, regardless of their starting points or individual circumstances. Our school culture, built upon high expectations for all, ensures that our students flourish. This not only means students achieving strong examination results but also developing their wider skills and talents, character, sense of belonging and civic duty. Our core values of respect, excellence and responsibility underpin everything we do, and apply to everyone in the school community, children and adults alike. Our teachers and support staff are well-qualified and committed professionals, who work tirelessly to provide great experiences and outcomes for all our students. As a result, students regularly achieve results which place us in the top cohort of schools nationally. We have also achieved nationally recognised awards for aspects of our work including attendance, professional development and wellbeing, whilst our students have won prestigious honours such as the DebateMate trophy. Unsurprisingly, we are one of the most popular schools in Newham.
Relationships between staff and students are built upon respect and understanding; behaviour is very good. We aim for our students to leave Stratford School Academy as knowledgeable, resilient, confident, articulate and well-rounded individuals, with a strong moral compass and in control of their destinies, thus empowered to make a positive contribution in a changing world.
I hope our website gives you a flavour of life at Stratford School Academy and invite you to browse the pages of the prospectus and watch our virtual tours. To keep up with the latest exciting news from the school please follow us on social media at:
X: @StratfordSch Instagram: stratford_school_academy

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission, Vision & Values - Stratford School Academy
pageCache.text:
Mission, Vision & Values
To serve our local community by providing every child with the knowledge, qualifications and wider experiences they need to develop to their potential and to participate in and make a positive contribution to society.
These are the deeply held beliefs that will provide the foundation for our school and guide every decision within it. These will not change over time and will underpin and inform our approach to all significant issues within the school. They should be ‘lived’ not just words on a website or letterhead, so should influence the way we do things on a day to-day basis. The chosen core values strongly reflect feedback from staff, students and parents, they are:
What this means at SSA
We show respect for ourselves and each other in everything we do; diversity is celebrated; we respect the environment, we respect learning
We aim for excellence in everything we do – teachers teach excellent lessons, students produce excellent work; we maintain a growth mindset and challenge ourselves and others to constantly strive for excellence
We all take responsibility for our actions, owning both our successes and those times we fall short; as a community, we recognise our responsibilities to each other and the wider community and environment

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 8 Enjoy French Theatre Experience - News - Stratford School Academy
pageCache.text:
Year 8 Enjoy French Theatre Experience
On Friday 6th February, all Year 8 students had the exciting opportunity to attend a live French/English theatre performance titled “Shipwrecked en France”, organised by our French Department. The play took place in the Assembly Hall during Period 1 for UL and Period 5 for GR.
The performance was thoroughly enjoyed by all students and provided a fantastic opportunity to experience French in a fun, interactive, and engaging way. Several students showed great confidence by volunteering to come up on stage and participate in the performance.
Students were also fully engaged throughout, eagerly helping to translate words from English into French when prompted by the actors. This interactive element helped to reinforce their learning and encouraged them to use their language skills in a real-life context.
Experiences like this play an important role in bringing language learning to life, helping students build confidence, improve their listening skills, and develop a greater appreciation for French language and culture.
We would like to thank the French Department for organising this memorable and enriching experience for our Year 8 students.

pageCache.text:
PSHCE
Our PSHCE curriculum aims to develop our students as responsible citizens who can make positive and meaningful contributions to their local communities and the wider world. We provide opportunities for students to understand elements of the modern world that they will need to make decisions about, offering valuable information so informed and safe decisions can be made.
KS3
At Key Stage 3 students are given opportunities to think critically about key issues that affect young people; enabling them to take part in important discussions, where different opinions are considered and questions are encouraged, to address misconceptions. Students reflect on their own beliefs, religious or otherwise, that informs their perspective on life and their interest in and respect for diversity. We teach students to respect and appreciate all forms of diversity within school and further afield, as an essential element of their preparation for life in the modern world.
In PSHCE lessons we explore key themes including Staying Safe, Personal Identity, Civil Rights and Healthy Relationships. A lesson will always focus one of our central themes and include students revisiting key areas throughout KS3, asking questions, and debating key elements of the area of study in a safe space.
We have designed our PSHCE curriculum to be specific to the needs, interests, and experiences of our students. We promote the spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of students so that they are prepared for life beyond secondary school. Students are taught to recognise the difference between right and wrong and to readily apply this understanding in their own lives. To recognise legal boundaries and, in doing so, respect the law of England. Students understand the consequences of their behaviour and actions and develop an interest in investigating and offering reasoned views about moral and ethical issues and ability to understand and appreciate the viewpoints of others on these issues.
Learning in PSHCE is supported by the pastoral system, other curriculum areas and other aspects of our school. Daily registration sessions and weekly assemblies continue the conversation around current local and global issues.
We encourage our students to develop their learning beyond the classroom by participating in extra-curricular clubs, such as debating. The PSHCE curriculum offers experiences that go beyond the classroom, with trips and visits by external agencies that help students to think critically about the wider world and the contributions that they will making. This is organised throughout the year to continue the conversations our curriculum provokes.
We want our students to leave SSA with a greater understanding of the world they live in and how they can use their voices to make a difference.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Powerful Learning Experience for Year 9 Students - News - Stratford School Academy
pageCache.text:
A Powerful Learning Experience for Year 9 Students
This term, all Year 9 students at SSA were treated to a visit from the Solomon Theatre Company, who performed their impactful production Skin Deep.
The play tackled important and sensitive topics such as knife crime, gang involvement, grooming, racism and peer pressure — issues that many young people may encounter, making the performance both relevant and educational. Delivered in an engaging and age-appropriate way, the production encouraged students to reflect, ask questions and think carefully about the choices they make.
We are delighted to share that the theatre company praised our students for being a fantastic audience — well-behaved, highly engaged and proactive in discussions, which is a real credit to them and to the school community.
Well done to all our Year 9s for representing SSA so positively, and a huge thank you to the staff who supported the students throughout the day and helped make this experience so meaningful.

pageCache.text:
Girls’ PE Reward Trip: An Unforgettable Night at the Copper Box Arena
Students from the Girls’ PE programme enjoyed an exciting reward trip to the Copper Box Arena to watch the London Lions in action. The evening was a fantastic experience, giving students the chance to soak up the electric atmosphere of live, professional basketball.
The game itself was thrilling, and the students loved seeing such a high level of skill and competition up close. One of the standout moments of the evening came during a timeout when one of our students was selected to take part in a shoot-out challenge on the court. She rose to the occasion brilliantly, winning the competition and earning a London Lions T-shirt to the cheers and applause of the crowd.
The trip was a huge success and a well-deserved reward for the students, who represented the school with enthusiasm and pride throughout the evening.
A special thank you goes to Ms Ali and Mr Godwin for accompanying Ms Heron and helping to ensure the trip ran smoothly.

pageCache.pageTitle: UKMT Junior Maths Challenge at Our School - News - Stratford School Academy
pageCache.text:
UKMT Junior Maths Challenge at Our School
Students at our school recently took part in the UKMT Junior Maths Challenge, a national mathematics competition organised by the UK Mathematics Trust. Aimed at students in Years 7 and 8, the challenge encouraged the development of mathematical reasoning, problem-solving skills, and logical thinking.
The competition consisted of 25 multiple-choice questions, completed within 60 minutes without the use of calculators. The questions were designed to be accessible while gradually increasing in difficulty, allowing all students to build confidence and enjoy mathematics, while also providing a challenge for more able participants.
We were delighted to host this exciting event and were proud of the enthusiasm and effort shown by all students who took part in this nationally recognised competition.
Congratulations to all participants for their hard work and commitment.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stratford School Academy Students Explore Fashion Careers at UAL London College of Fashion - News - Stratford School Academy
pageCache.text:
Stratford School Academy Students Explore Fashion Careers at UAL London College of Fashion
Students from Stratford School Academy recently visited the London College of Fashion (University of the Arts London) for an immersive careers workshop exploring the intersection of fashion, music, and creative identity.
Inspired by the college's Resonant Matter exhibition, students were challenged to consider what "joyful resistance" means to them and to style a look for an imaginary band's album cover, a creative brief that brought together personal expression, critical thinking, and hands-on design. A selection of the album covers they produced can be seen below.
The visit was led by two fashion lecturers from the college, who guided students around the campus and exhibition and supported them in thinking about the wide range of careers available in the fashion industry, including styling, modelling, photography, and more. An undergraduate student also spoke to the group about her own journey into fashion, offering practical guidance on planning next steps after secondary school, including advice on building a portfolio, pursuing internships, and choosing subjects at post-16 level.
Students left the workshop with an expanded understanding of what a career in fashion can look like and a renewed confidence in their own creative voices.
One student reflected: "Instead of speaking with your mouth, fashion can help you speak with your clothes. You can express the way you feel with your outfit.
Fashion and music are my biggest interests, and I love to think about the way they intersect to create identities that so many people identify with and find community in."
Another added: "Fashion comes in multiple opportunities, like styling, modelling, and photography."
The visit forms part of Stratford School Academy's wider careers programme, which provides students with meaningful encounters with employers and further and higher education providers to support their planning for life beyond secondary school. Thank you to UAL for hosting such an insightful visit, we look forward to visiting again.

pageCache.pageTitle: Green Careers Week - News - Stratford School Academy
pageCache.text:
Green Careers Week
Students Explore the Future of Work During Green Careers Week
From 3rd to 7th November, students in Years 7–10 took part in a wide-ranging programme of activities to mark Green Careers Week, an initiative designed to raise awareness of the growing demand for environmentally focused careers and the positive impact these roles have in addressing the climate crisis.
Throughout the week, students engaged in assemblies and reflective form-time activities exploring how their future qualification choices and personal skill sets could support pathways into green careers. These sessions encouraged students to think critically about how different industries are adapting and how they themselves can contribute to a more sustainable future.
A highlight of the week included welcoming Mo and Suzi from the Department of Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), who delivered workshops to Year 9 and 10 Geography classes. Their sessions offered valuable insights into the work of the Civil Service, the role of DESNZ, and the department’s efforts to drive national progress towards net-zero emissions. Students gained a clearer understanding of how government-led environmental initiatives are shaping the UK's future.
To round off the week, Year 8 students visited the London Stadium, where they learned how project managers and sustainability teams are working to reduce the stadium’s carbon footprint. Students toured several behind-the-scenes areas of the venue and discovered the wide range of green-focused careers involved in running and maintaining a major sports and events facility.
One student, Nichita (8UL1), said:
“I found the trip to London Stadium really nice; it was a great experience. There were many jobs at the stadium and some interesting jobs.”
Green Careers Week provided students with a meaningful opportunity to explore how innovation, sustainability, and career aspirations intersect—empowering them to imagine the roles they might play in building a greener future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stratford School Academy Achieves National Recognition for Outstanding Performance - News - Stratford School Academy
pageCache.text:
Stratford School Academy Achieves National Recognition for Outstanding Performance
Stratford School Academy is proud to announce that it has been recognised by SSAT (The Schools, Students and Teachers Network) in this year’s Educational Outcomes Awards. This national award places the school among the highest-performing secondary schools in the country, based on the latest performance data.
Stratford School Academy was recognised for being in the top 20% of non-selective schools nationally for student attainment in the 2025 end of KS4 exams.
The awards are based on analysis from SSAT’s Educational Outcomes Database, which combines data from DfE and Ofsted to compare performance across all state-funded schools in the country.
Receiving a SSAT Educational Outcomes Award is a significant achievement and reflects the dedication, expertise and commitment of the entire school community.
Sue Williamson, Chief Executive of SSAT, commented:
“Congratulations to Stratford School Academy on winning an SSAT Educational Outcomes Award. This success is down to the superb learning and teaching, outstanding support and inspirational leadership of staff. You have made a huge difference to the lives of the young people in your school. Thank you.”
SSAT is a membership organisation, bringing together schools and academies from across the UK and globally committed to achieving deep social justice. SSAT offers insight and understanding into school practice and educational policy and research. Their professional development and school improvement programmes help leaders and teachers to further outcomes for all young people and develop leadership at all levels across the system.
SSAT does this by providing a framework for exceptional education focused on teaching and learning, professional practice and leadership. This framework is underpinned by a commitment to social justice; the belief that every young person should go on to lead successful and fulfilling lives.
